_leia: ALL CHARACTER LINES, in English. Edit here: the game reads this file (src/game/i18n/i18n.ts merges it into locales/en.json). Each character has a 'filosofia' (reference only: the game does not read it) and the 'falas', keyed by the path the code asks for (e.g. 'wizard.intro'). Each line is one string; a leading '[narrator] ' makes it narration. {n} is replaced by a number. A backslash-n (\n) inside a line breaks the verse; a section with 'verso' is a poem, and src/game/i18n/versos.test.ts checks it against the Portuguese. The Portuguese file (pt-br.json) must have the same paths and the same number of lines in each speech.

_verso.nota: EVERY LINE IS VERSE: common meter (8·6·8·6 syllables, the ballad and hymn stanza), lines 2 and 4 rhyming, ONE STANZA PER BOX like the Portuguese (the whole quatrain together, so the rhyme is seen); a short line, or one the code slots into another, is a rhyming couplet (8·8). A poem of its own, not a translation: rhyme does not translate. The tests check that the boxes match the Portuguese; the meter is checked by ear.

filosofia.livros: Jean-Paul Sartre: Existentialism Is a Humanism (existence precedes essence; man is nothing but what he makes of himself), Being and Nothingness (condemned to be free). The hero does not speak: the narrator says it at the planted sword and at the end.
filosofia.ideia: No one is born with a meaning: you make it by what you do.
filosofia.voz: The hero does not speak. He was only a warrior; without the war, he remakes himself helping each neighbour.
filosofia.nome: Zero: Sartre's man begins with no essence, from nothing (Being and Nothingness), and only then is what he makes of himself. Sword laid down, he starts again from zero.

filosofia.livros: Siddhartha Gautama: the Dhammapada (276 the Buddhas only point the way), Majjhima Nikaya 22 (the parable of the raft: it is for crossing, not for carrying on your back), the Anattalakkhana Sutta (non-self: no role is what we are), the Benares sermon (the four noble truths: suffering comes from craving), the Anapanasati Sutta (the breath)
filosofia.ideia: Suffering comes from attachment; everything passes, and the way is to let go and be compassionate.
filosofia.voz: Few words, unhurried. Tells him to let go of the sword and care for others.
filosofia.nome: Sati is "mindfulness" in Pali, the first word of the Anapanasati Sutta, the breath he teaches the hero. It is being in what is here now, without the war that passed.

intro:
[narrator] The war is over. What remains
is road, and quiet air.

Your sword was just the raft you crossed;
don't haul it everywhere.

Now go and find what follows on:
the crossing's not the end.
Look after those who live here; then
the garden opens, friend.

You haven't truly slept, not once,
since all the war began.
Your camp is east, beyond the lake:
go rest there, if you can.

So go. Your sword can stay behind;
it's planted in the ground.

[narrator] Z talks and picks things up; and X
uses what you have found.
guide:
There's nothing left to fight. The war
has ceased; it isn't anymore.

The warrior was never you,
just what you used to do.
I only point the way. Meaning
is made by walking through.
again:
She comes again. Go back to sleep,
and sleep until the day.
I only point the road. Meaning:
you make it, come what may.
gate:
The garden's open. Have no dread:
its central fire lies ahead.
after:
You found it: just a place to sit,
with nothing else to do.
To suffer is to want what goes.
Breathe. Here the road is through.
tent:
There's nothing left to fight. The war
has ceased; it isn't anymore.

The warrior was never you,
just what you used to do.
I only point the way. Meaning
is made by walking through.

Rest at your camp, east of the lake;
go on now, find your bed.
The night is yours at last; your sleep
is waiting there ahead.

npc.wizard.name: Sati
lines:
There's nothing left to fight. The war
has ceased; it isn't anymore.

The warrior was never you,
just what you used to do.
I only point the way. Meaning
is made by walking through.

filosofia.livros: Laozi: Tao Te Ching (33 and 46 who knows enough is rich; 78 water overcomes stone). Zhuangzi (ch. 1 and 4 the useless tree, which lives long because no one cuts it; ch. 3 Cook Ding, who cuts along the joints and his knife never dulls)
filosofia.ideia: Follow the way of nature without forcing (wu wei), and know when it is enough.
filosofia.voz: Calm, watches what is unseen. Forces nothing: cut, do not pull; four are enough.
filosofia.nome: Shui is "water" in Chinese (水): "the highest good is like water", serving all without contending (Tao Te Ching 8), and "nothing is softer than water, yet nothing better overcomes stone" (78).

npc.radiationSuit.name: Shui
lines:
I watch the fungi of this vale:
they're slow, and they are right.
What shows is only fruit; the rest
is thread, and out of sight.

Eight kinds grow here; I need just four,
the others, if you please.
So take my knife and basket too,
and go among the trees.

npc.radiationSuitDone.name: Shui
lines:
Four is enough. Who knows enough
has everything they need.
Be water: soft, and yet the stone
gives way; the soft succeed.

The others, if you like, complete;
the red one you must never eat.

npc.radiationSuitAll:
All eight! You moved the way the vale
moves, never against it.
The red one's useless; so it lives
so long. Don't eat a bit.

porcini:
Right here, upon my left: cut this,
and learn how it is done.
Cut low, right at the ground, and slow:
the hurry? There is none.
morel:
Up north, an island holds a cap
of honeycomb, alone.
Two sticks will make a bridge to it;
the axe is Marco's own.
puffball:
Northeast, in the tall grass: a ball,
all white, without a cap.
Tall grass will fall to scythe or fire,
that opens up a gap.
inkCap:
Far north, behind the bushes, dry:
white, tall, and wild of hair.
A dry bush, set on fire, will burn
and clear a pathway there.
chanterelle:
Up north, in lava's ring: a gold
and funnel-shaped one, low.
A stone sinks down and turns to ground;
a stick held there will glow.
flyAgaric:
Northwest, past lava, brush: a red
with spots of white on top.
Bring stones and axe. Don't eat it:
it's poison, every drop.
oyster:
Out east, among the moonflowers,
it grows in shelves of grey.
Look for the tree that's dead and dry:
it eats that wood away.
jackOLantern:
West of the fallen ship, there grows
a glow when day is done.
Go out at night and follow it;
it's poison: eat not one.

finds.door.radiationSuit:
Best not come in: there's fungus all
over, even the chair.
The porch is yours. Sit down, and I'll
bring tea for you out there.

filosofia.livros: Albert Camus: The Myth of Sisyphus (the absurd: the silent world facing the one who asks for meaning; revolt, freedom and passion; the freedom of living without hope; the chapter "Absurd Creation": "to create is to live twice"; "one must imagine Sisyphus happy"), Summer ("Return to Tipasa": "in the midst of winter, I found there was, within me, an invincible summer")
filosofia.ideia: The world does not answer whoever asks it for meaning: that is the absurd. You do not escape it, neither by hope nor by despair: you live and create inside it, eyes open. The work saves nothing, and that is why it matters.
filosofia.voz: Starts in grey and ends in the colour she made herself, without promising the grey will not return. Celebrates those who create anyway.
filosofia.nome: Sisi, a nickname from Sisyphus: "one must imagine Sisyphus happy" (The Myth of Sisyphus). She lives the back and forth of the bucket.

npc.painter.name: Sisi
lines:
Whatever I paint comes out grey;
colour comes from the ground.
Take this shovel; dig the four cracks
right by me, in the ground.

npc.painterDone.name: Sisi
lines:
Your painting stays here, by my side,
where all its colours wake.
In winter's midst, I found in me
a summer none could break.

The grey comes back? Then let it come.
I paint, and pay the price.
Colour is my revolt, and so:
creating's living twice.

dig:
Still {n} to dig, and only where
the ground is cracked: just dig them there.
seeds:
Four holes! The shovel stays right here,
beside me, leaning there.
Mixed seeds: put one in every hole,
and plant each one with care.
sow:
One seed in every hole, and then:
{n} more, and colour starts again.
bucket:
Back, forth, and back, and never through:
you can imagine happy, too.
water:
Still {n} to water. Fill it up
and pour it slowly, cup by cup.
wait:
Now all there is to do is wait,
or sleep a night away:
by morning they'll be ready, all,
for you to pick, by day.
harvest:
They bloomed! Now pick all four by hand,
no tools: just hands, and care.
Then bring them to the table, all:
the paint is made right there.
bring:
Take flowers to the table: there
they turn to paint, and something rare.
easel:
Brush in your hand: now paint the world
you'd want, with every colour swirled.

intro:
What flowers! Watch how this is done,
and slowly, step by step, each one.
urucum:
Annatto: rubbed in water, seed
lets go its warm red powder, freed.
anil:
Indigo: leaves ferment; I beat,
and in the air the blue's complete.
curcuma:
Turmeric: the root, dried, milled fine,
becomes a yellow, like sunshine.
garanca:
Madder: ground root; and boiling, too,
turns all its red a darker hue.
binder:
Alum fixes the colour; and
gum makes it paint, for any hand.
brush:
Thank you for all the paints! I'll set
the canvas up; and so,
here, take the brush: the one who makes
is you now. Off you go.

Paint without hoping, and you'll stand
free, with an open, unarmed hand.

form.sparse:
A few strokes, and it says it all;
the white around is quiet, small.
form.middle:
Look what you did! This canvas shows
it all at once, the way it flows.
form.full:
Not one blank corner left in sight!
The canvas runs, a river, bright.

color.all:
All four colours: a courage I
did not have, painting earth and sky.
color.urucum:
That orange is late afternoon:
the low sun, burning, setting soon.
color.anil:
That blue is water, deep and wide:
look in, and you will sink inside.
color.curcuma:
That yellow's warmth is in the air:
it warms the canvas everywhere.
color.garanca:
That red has got a heart, and so
it beats upon the canvas, slow.

thanks:
You have a painter's hand. I saw
just grey; but colour's new:
we made it up, the two of us;
it's better done by two.

The painting stays here, where it's at;
the brush I keep, and that is that.

finds.door.painter:
In here, it's all wet paint, still fresh,
still dripping on the floor.
Sit on the porch: I'll bring the tea;
the view's worth waiting for.

filosofia.livros: Epictetus: Enchiridion (1 what is up to us; 5 judgements, not things; 11 "I gave it back", never "I lost it"). Seneca: Letters to Lucilius (1 only time is ours). Marcus Aurelius: Meditations (4.1 a strong fire turns what falls on it into more flame; 5.20 the obstacle becomes the way) Marcus Aurelius too: Meditations 4.40 (one universe, one nature).
filosofia.ideia: Separate what is up to us from what is not, and live in accordance with nature.
filosofia.voz: Lost what he did not control; holds on to what he does, a fire. Dry, working sentences.
filosofia.nome: Marco, after Marcus Aurelius, the Stoic emperor of the Meditations, whom he quotes on fire (4.1) and on the one nature (4.40).

npc.businessMan.name: Marco
lines:
I lost my business, firewood, all;
my hands won't stop their shake.
The rest is not mine. But a fire:
that one is mine to make.

Look for a dead tree, like this one:
no leaf, and grey, and dry.
Then chop a branch off with the axe;
bring it to me, close by.

Here, to the right, you'll see the stump:
stand the dead branch up tall;
then split it with the axe. Clean, rough:
it doesn't count at all.

The halves go to the ground; four times.
But look around with care:
dead trees are rare round here; so walk,
and search, and don't despair.

npc.businessManDone.name: Marco
lines:
I smell the smoke still. What weighs down
is not the things we meet:
it's what we think of them. My hands
are warm now, in the heat.

Thea, the sky; and I, the fire:
it's all one nature, true.
Thank you, my friend. The axe is yours;
I'm giving it to you.

gather:
Still {n} to go: dead branch, then stump,
then ground; and that's the way.
Dead trees are rare: so look around,
and search, and you won't stray.
block:
You've got a branch? Then see the stump,
right here, there on the right.
Stand the branch up on top of it:
upright, and set it tight.

Once it stands up, your axe will split
the branch in halves, clean through.
The halves go to the fire's ground:
that's all you have to do.
ready:
Four. That's a fire already; all
it needs is just a spark.
Go on and light it: all the wood
is split. Go light the dark.
light:
Go on, and light the fire there:
the wood is waiting, split with care.

split.clean:
Split clean. You've got a steady hand;
even the wood would understand.
split.rough:
Split crooked, but it split, and so:
you learn by striking. Now you know.

fire.first:
And it lit on the first strike, too:
a steady spark, and aimed and true.
fire.worked:
The fire was work; I know, I know:
all fires are; that's the way they go.

story:
Sit. Watch the fire with me, the way
you'd watch a friend at end of day.

A fire's not a thing: it's something
that happens, in plain sight.
The heat draws gas out of the branch:
the gas, not wood, alight.

The gas meets air, and burning gives
more heat, which frees more gas:
that's why it doesn't stop; alone,
it burns on, as hours pass.

And all that light? It's soot, it's grains
so hot, they start to glow.
A tree stores sun its whole life long;
the fire lets it go.

A strong fire turns what falls in it
to flame, all that it meets.
And life's the same: what blocks your way
is fuel the fire eats.
farewell:
Don't ever say 'I lost it.' Say
'I gave it back.' And so,
my hands don't shake. This night, at least,
is mine; I won't let go.

finds.door.businessMan:
The door is stuck; the porch is not:
it's yours to take, for free.
Sit down; I'll bring a cup of tea,
and some good company.

filosofia.livros: Aristotle: Metaphysics (I.1 all men by nature desire to know; I.2 wonder at the moon and the stars), Physics (II.3 the four causes: matter, form, maker and end), Nicomachean Ethics (I.7 one swallow does not make a summer; II.1 we become builders by building; IX.4 a friend is another self; X.7-8 the life of looking and the life of making, both after living well)
filosofia.ideia: Every human being desires to know; the happiest life is the contemplative one.
filosofia.voz: Curious and patient: the sky, the lens, Galileo. Meaning is in looking and understanding.
filosofia.nome: Thea, from theoria, contemplation, the life of looking in Nicomachean Ethics X.7. Theia is also the Greek titaness of sight and light.

npc.astronaut.name: Thea
lines:
Hello. My ship came down and broke;
I have to get back home.
Will you help me? Alone, I can't:
the sky's too wide to roam.

With the telescope whole, I'd know
where every star is set,
and where to send my signal; then
my friends would find me yet.

But in the fall, the telescope
broke too; just the tube stayed.
No tripod and no lens: the sky
has gone, the way things fade.

And all of us are born like this:
wanting to know. And so,
here, take this pickaxe; bring to me
an iron bar. Now go.

npc.astronautDone.name: Thea
lines:
The sky's still there: to look at it
is life's best part, by far.
Come back at night: a cairn of stones,
to show you where you are.

Marco lives making; I, by looking;
both seek to live life well.
Each has a way of reaching it,
and each one does it well.

One swallow doesn't make a summer,
and joy is not a day;
it is a whole life, all of it,
not half of it, halfway.

ore:
Go west, as far as lava goes:
the veins lie past the heat.
Break stones with no vein, toss them in:
they cool beneath your feet.

Look there for stones with veins: black gives
you coal, red gives you ore.
Just break the stone and pick it up:
that's what the pick is for.

The furnace here will only take
one thing at a time: no mistake.
bloom:
Coal and ore go to the furnace
right here; it tells you which
is missing; and you bring it: one
by one, without a hitch.
iron:
The anvil, here beside the flame:
the hot lump, hammered, takes its frame.

tripod:
Iron! This becomes the tripod.
The lens is missing: glass,
and glass is made of sand and ash:
the ash helps melt the mass.

The ash lies by the fire; the sand,
beside the big lake, south.
Both of them go into the furnace,
one open, waiting mouth.
polish:
Good glass! Now it becomes a lens:
the rough stone gives the curve;
the fine one clears the haze away,
and leaves it clear to serve.

Rub it in circles, round and round,
until the lens is clear and sound.
carry:
It's sharp! The matter is the sand,
the form, the lens; and you,
the maker; seeing is the end.
Now carry it on through

to the plateau, southwest: climb up
the stairs, to find the mark.
Up there, the sky is clean and whole:
a dome, clear in the dark.
night:
By day, you can't see anything.
Sit by it, through the gray,
for night to come, without a rush:
the sky loves those who stay.
reunion:
I saw the fire from way up high.
Any marshmallows left? Oh my!
goodbye:
With the sky back, my ship found me.
Thank you for everything:
a friend is another self; I'll take
you with me, wandering.

But I must go back to my planet:
my home is up on high.
When you look up at night, just wave:
it brings us close, the sky.
farewell:
You found all four! The wonder at
the moon and stars, I'd say,
first made us think: philosophy
was born from it that way.

The light you saw was on its way
long, long before your birth;
it only needed someone's eyes
to look at it from earth.

The stars before the dawn are new:
so sleep, and then arise,
and wake up early for them: there,
the season turns the skies.
anvil:
The bar! Nobody's born a smith:
you make one, hammering.
And now I'll build the tripod: so
stay, watch me do the thing.

finds.door.astronaut:
The porch has the best view there is,
after my ship, I'd say.
Sit there: I'll bring the tea, and let
the hours drift away.

filosofia.escola: Nihilism, and its overcoming (Nietzsche, to the letter)
filosofia.livros: Friedrich Nietzsche: The Gay Science (§125 the death of God; §341 the eternal return), Thus Spoke Zarathustra (the three metamorphoses; the dancing star), Ecce Homo (amor fati; "become who you are")
filosofia.ideia: The highest values devalue themselves: nothing has a given meaning. The passive nihilist stops there; the active one tears down the idols (the lion) and creates new values playing (the child), and loves fate so much as to want it again, without end.
filosofia.voz: Calm, unthreatening. Three nights: diagnoses, tests, blesses. Never consoles; asks. Leaves the scythe on the first.

death.name: Death
visit:
Don't rise. I didn't come for you.
I know you, from the start:
I walked behind you through the war;
I never stood apart.

Wherever you went, I was there,
with all my work to do.
Tonight you sleep beneath the stars;
your sword sleeps in the dew.

Glory and honour, victory:
these were your gods. They're dead.
So nothing's worth a thing at all,
and no new gods instead.

No one will tell you what has worth;
the emptiness is yours.
Now sleep. There is no need to rush:
I've waited out your wars.
visit2:
Here once again. I said I'd wait.
You only did as told:
you carried orders on your back,
a camel, bought and sold.

Out in the desert, camels turn
to lions, roaring: no.
They tell the old gods no. But claws
aren't hands; they cannot sow.

And now, a question. Do not lie
to me. Do not pretend.
What if this life came back, the same,
each pain, each night, no end?

Would you curse me, the one who spoke,
or say: yes, all once more?
Don't answer now. Sleep on it, sleep.
I'm patient, as before.
visit3:
The final night. When it is done,
I won't come back to you.
The lion turns into a child,
forgets, and starts anew.

It says yes, and in play it makes
its values, asking none.
No one has given you a meaning:
your hands are making one.

Want nothing other, not ahead,
nor back, nor what could be.
Love all of it, the way it is,
for all eternity.

One must have chaos still within
to birth a dancing star.
Sleep well, child. This is my goodbye:
become the one you are.

ultimo_pedido.nota: Whoever closes the last request says this at the end of their own speech, and hands over the High Garden key.

garden.key:
You were a friend to everyone:
the village, and the wild.
Take the key: the High Garden is
yours. Walk there, soft and mild.

filosofia.livros: Epicurus (his school was called "The Garden"): Letter to Menoeceus (death is nothing to us: when it is, we are not), Principal Doctrines (27 friendship is the greatest good), Vatican Sayings (33 not hungry, not thirsty, not cold, rivals Zeus in happiness)
filosofia.ideia: Happiness is friendship, simple pleasures and the peace of needing nothing more.

ending.lines:
[narrator] The marshmallow goes gold; the sword
stays out there on the road.
No one has chosen for him; he
was made from what he sowed.

[narrator] No hunger, cold, and friends close by:
no god has more than this.
Death's nothing: when it comes, we're gone;
it's never ours to miss.

[narrator] No place to go, no need, no list:
at last, it's good just to exist.

narrador.nota: Not an NPC: things in the valley read with Z (finds, the camp).

finds.helmet:
[narrator] A helmet, rusted through. Inside,
a flower took its root,
without a by-your-leave, right where
the war had stamped its boot.
finds.bottle:
[narrator] A bottle, and a note inside:
“I made it. It's good here.”
“Come.” And no name. Whoever wrote
it left nothing else to hear.
finds.sword:
[narrator] This blade once overcame the dark;
it gave the world its light.
He is no longer this: he's what
he chooses now, outright.
finds.smithy:
[narrator] The old forge. Long ago, the smith
went off and never came.
The furnace still draws well today,
and waits for a new flame.
finds.sign:
[narrator] The High Garden: closed, to protect
the wild it holds within.
No one goes in, unless they've been
allowed to enter in.
finds.signOpen:
[narrator] The High Garden: closed, to protect
the wild it holds within.
No one goes in, unless they've been
allowed to enter in.

[narrator] Someone crossed out the “closed”: and so,
the path is open; in you go.
finds.door.empty:
[narrator] No one at home. The porch, though, stays,
for anyone who's tired,
who comes and sits a while, and asks
for nothing; none required.

ring:
[narrator] A ring of fire-stones, cold and grey,
that wait now for another day.
rack:
[narrator] Mushrooms are drying on the rack:
a gift from Shui, to bring her back.
easel:
[narrator] The painting Sisi made: the grey,
and then the colour, here to stay.
woodpile:
[narrator] Dry wood that Marco gave to you:
the fire is yours now, through and through.
chart:
[narrator] The map of stars that Thea drew,
her way, the way she always knew.

cat.barrel:
[narrator] A barrel lying down, with straw
inside. The one who stays
needs nothing more than what he has:
the sun, and his own days.

filosofia.livros: Diogenes of Sinope ("the dog"): through Diogenes Laertius, Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, book VI (20-21 deface the currency; 22 the mouse; 37 the bowl; 38 Alexander and the sun; 40 Plato's man; 41 the lantern; 49 the statue; 60 the dog; 63 citizen of the world and "ready for any fortune"; 105 the gods need nothing) And Diogenes Laertius, book VII.2: Zeno, who founded Stoicism, learned from Crates, a student of Diogenes.
filosofia.ideia: Happiness is self-sufficiency (autarkeia) and living according to nature. Custom, fame and wealth are false currency: deface them. Train body and will to need little, and speak the truth to anyone's face (parrhesia), without shame.
filosofia.voz: Mocking, lazy in the sun, unimpressed by heroes. Short and blunt. Accepts a pet and answers with a lesson.
filosofia.nome: Sinope is the city of Diogenes, the one that exiled him. He answered that he was a citizen of the world (Diogenes Laertius VI.63): the cat carries the name of the land he does not need.

npc.blackCat.name: Sinope
lines:
A hero. How new. So you'd like
to give me something? Fine:
then step out of my sun. That's all
I want; the sun is mine.

1:
A hero. How new. So you'd like
to give me something? Fine:
then step out of my sun. That's all
I want; the sun is mine.
2:
I learned to live by watching mice:
no bed is what they seek,
no fear of dark, no feast, no fame;
they eat, and sleep, and squeak.
3:
I saw a child drink from its hands;
I threw my bowl away:
that child had beaten me at being
more simple, plain as day.
4:
The gods need nothing; who needs little
is nearly one, I'd say.
And you, hero, tell me: how much
do you carry, each day?
5:
Where am I from? The world, all through:
a citizen of it; and you?
6:
They call me dog. I'm cat. A name
is nothing; never mind.
I purr for givers, hiss at those
who won't; claw the unkind.
7:
I walked by day, lamp in my hand,
to find a man. I came
on heroes, plenty; but a man?
Not one. And none to name.
8:
My advice: go deface the coin:
honour, glory, the norm;
cross it all out, and what is left
is you, without the form.
9:
I beg for food from statues: so
I train to get no meal.
Who hopes for nothing doesn't hurt:
the stone has taught me steel.
10:
Plato said man's a biped, one
without a feather, plain.
I plucked a chicken, brought it in:
“There's Plato's man!” Explain.
11:
What did philosophy give me?
To be ready for what may be.
12:
The woodsman lost it all, and learned
that little is enough.
A pupil of my pupil taught
many that very stuff.

fora_do_jogo.nota: NPCs from an old version: not in the current world.

npc.salesman.name: SALESMAN
lines: Friend! You look thirsty. Or dry. Either way — opportunity.
Free sample: this BUCKET. Fill it in my pond, just west of the fire.
A full bucket waters crops and drowns small fires. Endless uses. Costs you nothing. Today only.
Tell your friends. If you find any out there.

npc.poet.name: POET
lines: The pines sing, but they crowd the verse.
This GREAT AXE fells even LIVING trees — the small axe only knows dead wood.
Open a clearing in my grove. Listen how the song changes where light falls.
Every good line needs its silence. Cut me one.
